request: Restore per-tap hearts for ordinary own-Plushie interactions; retain held feedback during Touch Note recording; no simulator inspection

changes.controller: Only an active Touch Note input capture may produce periodic held feedback; ordinary touch-down still produces its existing single three-heart burst
changes.ordinary: Holding or dragging no longer adds timed heart/haptic bursts; release, new taps and Squeeze/Bonk retain their existing interaction behavior
changes.recording: First action and subsequent 500ms held counting/one visible heart remain unchanged; recording's internal toy particles remain hidden
changes.sharedScope: Same useSquishyToy controller for Skia and native fallback
unchanged: Moments durable queue and fixed one-hour aggregation
Touch Note duration, quota, send and replay

verification.counterexample: Before the controller fix, the new ordinary-held test failed with 12 particle births instead of 3; the corresponding recording test passed

lifecycle.note: Old ordinary 500ms expectation split into ordinary non-repeating and recording repeating cases; task/rating record protections retained

domain.note: Final complete rerun after updating the explicitly superseded ordinary-hold contract

verification.limits: Code/worklet/component-model tests only. Per user request, no simulator, screenshots, physical-device haptic verification or native performance sampling this turn. Targeted suites overlap the domain gate; counts are not additive.

release: Client-only source change, applies after Metro reload. No API/database deployment, App publication or Git commit. Existing unrelated working-tree changes preserved.
